scope: Bounded local check requested by Human Owner. No Study admission or publication.
window_selection: 2023 is the most recent complete non-leap calendar year before 2025. The local A0 sources located for this comparison contain no evaluation of 2023. No outcome data inspected before this record.
alternative_selection: Two symmetric flanks of +24 h, selected before download. +12 h corresponds to the IOTA half address and +36 h is 1.5 addresses.
source: JPL Horizons ELEMENTS, hourly TDB, 501/502/503 relative to 500@599, BODY EQUATOR; match 2025 jup365_merged when available and disclose any ephemeris difference
angle: Individual longitudes = round((OM + W + MA) modulo 360, 7); Laplace angle = (Io - 3*Europa + 2*Ganymede) modulo 360
grids: Prime integer hours in 0..8759. Uniform hours = nearest integer to i*8760/1092 for i=0..1091 with ties upward. Shift both grids modulo 8760 and sort.
scoring: Strict sign change of hourly Laplace angle around 180 degrees defines reference crossing. Count a crossing only if alone between successive sorted marks, with left mark < crossing hour <= right mark, and endpoints on opposite sides. Include hour 8760 in the hourly reference. Do not create a cyclic interval between last and first sampling marks.
primary_decision: For each lag subtract D count from shifted count per base and grid, across 12 pairs. Hypothesis supported in this window only if average prime difference at +24 h is positive and larger than average uniform difference. A nonpositive prime difference rejects direction for this window; equal or greater uniform gain leaves prime specificity unsupported.
specificity_decision: Compute the same prime-minus-uniform paired gain for +12 h and +36 h. +24 h is uniquely strongest among these controls only if it strictly exceeds both and passes the primary rule. No inferential claim from overlapping phases.
stop: No scoring if timestamps, common frame, or reference transitions cannot be verified; no data-dependent offset or year substitution.
